sections.h2: Owners, renters and who buys in Ithaca
sections.html:
Renters outnumber owners in this university city, and only 29.6% of homes are owner-occupied. So the first thing to settle before a sale is whether your house has ever been a rental. That answer shapes who will bid and what the city will want to see.

Ithaca sits at the south end of Cayuga Lake in Tompkins County. The Town of Ithaca around it is a separate municipality, so confirm which one covers your address. The city has 33,632 residents, up 4.8% from the 2020 base of 32,085, in 14,167 households of about 1.71 people. Just 54.2% of residents were in the same house a year earlier, which tells you how often homes change hands here. Decide early whether your likely buyer lives in the house, wants rental income, or pays cash and takes the place as is.

  • Owner-occupied houses on East Hill, West Hill and South Hill tend to sell to people planning to live in them.
  • Houses near Collegetown, or with accessory apartments, attract investors who will ask about the rental certificate.
  • Houses needing work or holding tenants often move fastest to a cash buyer.

The middle value of an owned home in the city is $342,700, and gross rent is $1,447 at the midpoint. Owners with a mortgage pay $2,368 a month, and those without one pay $994. Household income is $48,784 at the midpoint.

The city covers only 5.39 square miles of land, so housing is tight and a modest house can draw several showings in a good season. Buyers pay attention to walkable addresses, since the average commute is just 18.7 minutes and Cornell and Ithaca College supply most of the jobs. The hills matter too: East Hill, West Hill and South Hill each have their own feel, so ask an agent for sales on your own hillside.

If the house has accessory apartments or past student tenants, say so when you talk to buyers. Investors will price the rental paperwork into their offer, and owner-occupants will want to know what they are inheriting.

The city requires a housing inspection and a Certificate of Compliance for residential rentals, and a buyer who plans to rent will check that yours is current. The rule reaches one- and two-family dwellings, multiple dwellings, dormitories, fraternities, sororities, mixed-use buildings with apartments and accessory apartments in single-family homes.

Fees depend on building type. The Building Division bills the owner after the inspection, and payment is due within 30 days. Each property gets one 30-day extension to prepare for inspection or fix violations without added violation charges.

City of Ithaca Certificate of Compliance fees
Inspection itemFee

Short-term rentals need a permit in addition to the certificate. It lasts one year, the permit number goes in every listing, a local contact must answer within 60 minutes, and hosts collect a 5% Tompkins County occupancy tax and a 5% City of Ithaca one. If your buyer wants to run the house as a short-term rental, ask the Building Division at 108 E. Green Street whether the permit transfers or must be reissued. The housing inspection line is (607) 274-6509.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Tompkins County
sections.html:
The Tompkins County Clerk records deeds for Ithaca. The first page costs $50 and each added page $5. Residential deeds carry a $10 deed notice, and the TP-584 transfer tax return costs $5. Transfer tax is $6 per $1,000.

The RP-5217 real property transfer report costs $125 for residential property and $250 otherwise. A seller who lives out of state files form IT-2663, which the state revises every year, so use the current version. The clerk's counter takes cash or check.

Land record searches by clerk staff run $5 per name for records back to 1968, and copies are $0.65 a page with a $1.30 minimum. Your closing attorney or title company normally handles all of this. Just know that these Tompkins County amounts will not match a settlement statement from a sale elsewhere in New York.

Before closing, collect what the attorney will ask for: a copy of your deed, the current rental certificate if the house is a rental, any open violation notices, and your out-of-state form if it applies. Having these ready keeps the closing date from slipping while someone hunts for a document.

Snow averages about 67 inches a year, so buyer inspectors look closely at roofs, gutters, foundations and heating systems. Expect questions about the furnace's age, whether pipes in exterior walls have ever frozen and how water leaves the lot after spring melt. A house without air conditioning still sells, but it may draw a lower offer.

  • Gather heating, roof and foundation records before the first showing.
  • Photograph the house in dry weather if the basement ever took on water.
  • Clear gutters and walkways before an inspection in cold months.

sections.h2: Is a cash offer a good fit for an Ithaca house?
sections.html:
Cash fits houses with rental violations, deferred repairs or tenants in place, because those problems slow a financed sale. A clean owner-occupied house in a sought-after neighborhood may do better on the open market.

Get any offer in writing. Ask how the buyer handles an expired Certificate of Compliance or open violations, and have a New York real estate attorney review the contract. Compare the price with what you would net after commission, repairs and several months of carrying costs. A student rental adds a timing question, so ask the buyer up front how existing leases would be handled.

The steps for a cash sale are short. You accept a written offer, the attorney and title company order a title search, you sign the deed and transfer forms, and the buyer pays at closing. Because no lender is involved, there is no loan approval or appraisal to wait on. If the house has an expired certificate, you and the buyer decide in the contract who schedules the inspection and who pays the fees listed above.

faqs.q: Does Ithaca require a certificate before I sell a rental house?
faqs.a: The city requires a Certificate of Compliance for residential rentals, issued after a Building Division housing inspection. A buyer who will keep renting usually wants it current, so schedule the inspection early. Applications can be made online.

faqs.q: How much is a Certificate of Compliance for a one-family house in Ithaca?
faqs.a: The initial inspection is $100 for a one-family dwelling and $175 for a two-family. Each violation found adds $10 and each one still uncorrected at re-inspection costs $50. A return trip is $75 per hour with a $75 minimum.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Tompkins County?
faqs.a: The first page is $50 and each added page $5. Add a $10 deed notice, a $5 TP-584 filing and the $125 RP-5217 fee for residential property. Transfer tax is $6 per $1,000.

faqs.q: Which municipality covers my Ithaca address?
faqs.a: The City of Ithaca and the surrounding Town of Ithaca are separate municipalities. Check your tax bill or ask the city Building Division before you start city paperwork such as a rental certificate.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Ithaca house if it has an Airbnb permit?
faqs.a: Yes. Ask the Building Division whether a new owner must apply for a fresh permit. The permit lasts one year, depends on a current Certificate of Compliance, and hosts collect separate 5% city and county occupancy taxes.
